_meta.authored: AUTHORED from the engagement analysis, not captured from a client intake form. No raw intake form exists for this engagement. Form fields are reconstructed from statements in the source document; the derived competitive set and the expected conclusion are taken from it directly. The per-dimension expected levels are an ASSISTANT MAPPING of that conclusion onto the six calibrated dimensions - they are not a recorded client label. The BAND, not the dimension vector, is the bar (spec 10.6).
_meta.expected_conclusion: CBD saturated at every tier; white space outside it (spec 10.1)
_meta.notes: CBD crowded at both the top and the value tier - ~45+ CBD locations fighting for the same white-collar lunch. SaladStop! owns health/wellness, Supergreen owns best value, Six Hands owns 'healthy that doesn't feel like a sacrifice', OMNIVORE owns Thai/SEA flavor; hawker stalls own S$5-9. Heartland is underserved at premium but owned at value by Stuff'd (36 branches, ~24k reviews, S$8-13, ~27 non-CBD malls). Evidence base: 12,523 verified Google reviews.
_meta.pre_launch_caveat: PRE-LAUNCH CASE. As with C4, the engagement's conclusion is about the MARKET rather than a position held, so the band under-expresses it. The instrument's honest reading of an unlaunched venture is Fragile regardless of how good the untaken position looks - which is the behaviour this case is here to lock down.

form.category: Salad and healthy-bowl quick-service restaurants in Singapore - lunch-led, CBD-first, then island-wide.
form.positioning_sentence: A beautiful, protein-forward, filling healthy bowl - healthy that actually tastes like a treat.
form.differentiator: We are building the bowl as an object of desire rather than a diet food. Visual presentation engineered to be striking, in the way Tokyo Salad Bowl does it, directly attacking the category's documented failure mode of the joyless watery salad. Protein-forward and genuinely filling, with published per-bowl macros synced to tracking apps, so it answers the 'not filling, small portion' complaint. We will operate in the heartland, where the premium healthy-bowl tier is genuinely thin, rather than fighting for CBD lunch traffic.
form.undercut_on: Value and location. Stuff'd sells a filling bowl at S$8-13 across 36 branches, and hawker stalls do the same job for S$5-9. We are not the cheapest way to eat lunch, and ready-to-eat supermarket salads undercut us at about S$5.
form.your_price_point: Premium healthy bowl, above the S$8-13 value tier.
form.their_price_point: Hawker stalls S$5-9; Stuff'd S$8-13; supermarket ready-to-eat salads about S$5; meal-prep subscriptions S$8-15 per meal.

customer_description: CBD white-collar lunch buyers first, then heartland diners. Health-aware office workers who want a lunch that is both healthy and satisfying, and who currently choose between a joyless salad and something they actually want to eat.

derived_competitive_set.derivation_method: Derived from the SG salad and healthy-bowl category: outlet counts across CBD and non-CBD malls, published price tiers, and the pain/praise structure across 12,523 verified reviews.

members: a non-salad lunch - rice, noodles, a sandwich
tier_0_default.why: Most lunches are not salads, and the category competes against the whole lunch set.

tier_1_cheap_substitute.price_floor: S$5-9 for a full lunch undercuts any premium bowl.
tier_1_cheap_substitute.why: This rung is where the value buyer actually eats, and the online meal-prep trend competes for the same wallet.

tier_2_direct_set.why: These compete for the same health-conscious lunch at a similar price.

tier_3_category_incumbent.diagnostic: SaladStop! owns 'health and wellness' in this category. It has only about 4 non-CBD stores and treats delivery as an add-on channel, which is the gap a heartland entrant can use.
tier_3_category_incumbent.why: It is the reference occupant of the salad category in Singapore.

tier_4_adjacent_crossover.why: A burrito, poke bowl or flavoured rice bowl solves the same lunch need and often more cheaply.

members: none - no intermediary specifies a lunch venue
tier_5_professional_route.why: There is no professional gatekeeper in this category.

members: HPB Healthier Dining grant shaping menus
tier_6_indirect.why: A workplace catering contract can remove the individual lunch decision entirely.

_expected.why: A pre-launch venture with no name, no outlets and no customers. Fragile. Its conclusion ('CBD saturated at every tier; white space outside it') is a landscape statement, recorded here as competitive_room 3 - the CBD is saturated at both ends even though the specific beautiful-protein-bowl position is unclaimed. This case most directly tests whether the instrument rewards an unclaimed WORD over a held POSITION: the position is open, the business holds nothing.
